title: 09 · StoryMaps — guided
summary: Follow census blocks between economic regions and health areas, see where the links are incomplete, and learn how to connect regional indicators without changing their meaning.
sourceNote: Statistics Canada 2021 SGC membership; existing Ministry/BCCDC 2021 DB–CHSA crosswalk; BCMoH boundary snapshots; NDIT/MNP State of the North inventory (model refresh 2026-04-30). Health polygon vintage is not established as 2021. Crosswalk population covers its source DB universe, with 36 extra population records excluded by the upstream crosswalk. No dashboard rates are reallocated.
details: The same connected-geographies story presented with the slideshow editorial layout. This is a PGMaps implementation inspired by the supplied StoryMaps reference, using our own boundary sources and narrative.

The ID-based bridge retains one row per source census block and checks the official CSD/CD/economic-region memberships. It produces ER, CD and CSD comparisons with CHSA, LHA, HSDA and HA, including null parent groups.

Population shares are descriptive fractions of covered 2021 residents. They are not universally valid allocation weights for jobs, capacity, production, housing prices or rates. Medians cannot be aggregated by averaging.
The 533 unresolved blocks retain CHSA 2210 and null parents. Different CHSA code sets are documented in the manifest; no centroid assignment, code-prefix guess or silent replacement repairs them.

The dashboard registry describes every inspected entity and reviews seven pilot datasets. Only the vacancy pilot has explicit geography links in this release; its Northern B.C. group remains unverified. Other datasets require the work described in the joining guide.

links.label: Read the crosswalk and dashboard joining guide

scenes.label: One province, several maps
scenes.title: Different boundaries answer different questions
scenes.text: Economic regions describe regional economies. Census areas organize population statistics. Health areas organize services. They stay separate in the selector, while a crosswalk connects their IDs. Click an economic region to inspect its health links and coverage.

callout.label: Common joining unit
callout.detail: 2021 source crosswalk; not a current population estimate.

paragraphs: Start with the question you want to answer. Economic reporting, population statistics and health-service planning use different geographic units. The crosswalk lets us connect their identifiers while retaining those distinctions.

scenes.label: The census path
scenes.title: Prince George belongs to Cariboo economic region
scenes.text: The official 2021 classification links Prince George census subdivision 5953023 to Fraser-Fort George census division 5953 and Cariboo economic region 5950. The economic region also contains Cariboo census division 5941. Similar names do not mean identical boundaries.
paragraphs: Read this as an official membership path. A shared place name does not make an economic region, census division and municipality interchangeable. Select a map action to inspect the same path at a different scale.

scenes.label: The health path
scenes.title: The same blocks have a second address
scenes.text: Prince George block records link to community health service areas, then Prince George Local Health Area 524, Northern Interior Health Service Delivery Area 52 and Northern Health Authority 5. The map shows the repository health polygons; their vintage is not established as 2021.
paragraphs: The health hierarchy is a second classification of the same province. Use the actions below to reveal one level at a time. These display polygons provide context; the bridge itself follows the source block IDs.

scenes.label: Where the systems cross
scenes.title: One economic region can span several health authorities
scenes.text: Cariboo economic region has source blocks assigned to Northern, Interior and Vancouver Coastal health authorities. The bridge keeps every relationship, with covered population shares in both directions. Those shares describe residents; they do not tell us where jobs or industrial output occur.

callout.label: Relationship type
callout.detail: Filter the downloadable table to one census/health comparison before summing.

paragraphs: Move the divider, use its arrow keys, or choose either map. The comparison shows entire boundary systems at one camera position. Population shares come from the ID bridge, not from the apparent size of an overlap on screen.

scenes.label: The visible gap
scenes.title: An unresolved link remains visible
scenes.text: The source assigns 533 blocks, containing 78,916 residents, to CHSA 2210 but supplies no higher health-area links. That CHSA code is absent from the current local index, which instead contains different New Westminster CHSA codes. We show the current health polygons for context and retain the old assignment until a dated official concordance resolves it.

callout.label: Unresolved health parents
callout.detail: These records remain in every census-side denominator; they are never silently dropped.

paragraphs: An unresolved relationship is part of the result. Keeping these residents in the denominator makes missing links visible. The current New Westminster outlines shown here are context, not a reconstruction of the older CHSA assignment.

scenes.label: Bring in the indicators
scenes.title: Connect the geography before combining the numbers
scenes.text: The vacancy pilot links Cariboo and Northeast directly to economic regions. North Coast and Nechako is one combined reporting area: its value stays in one row with two member IDs. Northern B.C. remains unresolved until its table-specific definition is verified. Housing markets, ferry routes, mines and NDIT service regions each need their own joining rules.

highlights.label: North Coast and Nechako reporting group

callout.label: Available in Sources and downloads
callout.detail: 12 geography comparisons, a 41-entity dashboard registry and 866 linked vacancy pilot rows. Do not sum rates or average medians.

paragraphs: A geography match is only the first step. Before combining indicators, retain each measure’s reference period, units and native reporting area. The source guide explains the reviewed datasets and the remaining joining work.
